form.title: PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT

field.label: Financing
field.options: Cash, Bank, Owner, Blend, Show All

form.section: This Purchase and Sale Agreement is made as of the Effective Date between (the "Buyer") and (the "Seller"). Brokers named in this Agreement facilitate the transaction and are not parties to the sale covenants except for the limited broker acknowledgment on the signature page. Each Party represents it has capacity and authority to bind itself. If a Party is married under sociedad de gananciales, the spouse shall join this Agreement and the escritura unless a recorded capitulaciones or court order establishes otherwise. If a Party is an entity, it shall deliver good-standing and authority documents the Notary requires before Closing. Powers of attorney executed outside Puerto Rico shall be apostilled or consularized as the Notary requires.

Seller agrees to sell and Buyer agrees to buy the property known as , Municipality of , Catastro Number , Finca , Registry Section , Registry Entry (the "Property"), together with improvements and fixtures permanently attached to it, and any personal property listed in Additional Terms. The controlling legal description is the description in the last recorded escritura and the certified extract of the Registro de la Propiedad. A marketing name has no legal effect. Title shall be conveyed subject only to real-property taxes not yet due, recorded easements and servitudes that do not materially interfere with present use, association documents if any, and public coastal-zone and beach limitations of general application, plus exceptions Buyer does not timely object to (collectively, "Permitted Exceptions").

The purchase price is (the "Purchase Price"). The elected Transaction Type is . The Purchase Price is paid as follows: earnest money of held by ; cash due at Closing of ; institutional loan proceeds of ; and seller-carried principal of . Components that do not apply are completed as zero. The completed components plus the Deposit credited at Closing must equal the Purchase Price. Buyer shall pay in immediately available U.S. dollars, subject to prorations and required tax withholding.

Within three Business Days after the Effective Date, Buyer shall deliver the Deposit of by wire to . The Deposit is applied to the Purchase Price at Closing. It is refundable if Buyer timely terminates under a contingency this Agreement expressly treats as a refund-out (financing, appraisal if not waived, inspection, title, survey, casualty, condemnation, or Seller default). After those contingencies expire or are waived in writing, the Deposit is non-refundable except on Seller default. Neither Party shall rely on an email that changes wiring instructions. Wiring instructions shall be confirmed by a live telephone call to a number already known to the sender.

Closing means authorization of the escritura de compraventa before a Puerto Rico notary public, delivery of the Purchase Price net of credits and required withholdings, delivery of possession as provided herein, and presentation of the certified copy to the Registro de la Propiedad. Closing shall occur on or before before , or another Puerto Rico notary the Parties agree. The Closing Notary is a public officer and is not counsel for either Party. A mainland-style deed does not transfer Puerto Rico real property. Either Party may extend Closing by up to fifteen days if a title, Registry, or governmental certificate item is being cured in good faith. A longer extension requires a written amendment.

At Closing Seller shall convey good and marketable title, insurable at regular rates, free of liens other than Permitted Exceptions, by escritura publica acceptable for inscription. Seller shall cause a Puerto Rico title study and a standard title-insurance commitment to be delivered to Buyer at Seller's expense. Buyer shall give written title objections within ten days after receipt of the commitment. Seller shall have fifteen days to cure. Seller must cure monetary liens Seller created or assumed. If a timely objection is not cured and is not waived, Buyer may terminate and recover the Deposit. Seller shall deliver cancellation instruments needed to clear non-permitted liens and shall cooperate with presentation to the Registry.

Real-property taxes, CRIM charges, and municipal assessments shall be prorated as of the Closing Date. Seller shall pay items through the day of Closing and shall deliver a current CRIM certification of debt or evidence of payment arrangement acceptable to the Notary. Buyer pays items after Closing. Special assessments levied before the Effective Date are Seller's expense unless Additional Terms state otherwise.

section.title: Risk of Loss, Casualty and Condemnation

form.section: Risk of loss remains with Seller until Closing and passes to Buyer upon authorization of the escritura and delivery of possession. Seller shall maintain existing hazard coverage, and flood coverage if the Property is in a Special Flood Hazard Area, through Closing. If the Property suffers Material Casualty before Closing (repair cost exceeding five percent of the Purchase Price, or damage that cannot reasonably be repaired before Closing), Buyer may terminate and recover the Deposit, or proceed with assignment of insurance proceeds and a credit for any deductible. If any material part of the Property is taken or placed under a formal taking proceeding before Closing, Buyer may terminate and recover the Deposit or proceed and take the award.

Except for a failure to close on the Closing Date when time is of the essence and the other Party is ready, willing, and able, a Party is not in default until written notice and a five-day cure period have expired. If Buyer defaults, Seller may terminate and retain the Deposit as liquidated damages and not as a penalty. The Parties agree the Deposit is a reasonable pre-estimate of Seller's marketing, carrying, and opportunity losses. Retention of the Deposit is Seller's exclusive pre-Closing remedy for Buyer default. If Seller defaults, Buyer may terminate and recover the Deposit plus documented out-of-pocket title, survey, inspection, and lender fees, or seek specific performance, or terminate and pursue actual damages. Default under an owner-financed note after Closing is governed by that note and the hipoteca, not by the Deposit clause.

If Financing is Cash, Buyer's obligation to close is not conditioned on obtaining a loan. Failure to have immediately available funds on the Closing Date is a Buyer default. Within five Business Days after the Effective Date, Buyer shall deliver evidence reasonably acceptable to Seller that Buyer has liquid funds at least equal to the Purchase Price plus estimated Buyer-side closing costs. Seller shall keep that evidence confidential. Unless Appraisal Waived is No, any appraisal is for Buyer's information only and does not entitle Buyer to terminate or reprice. Buyer represents the funds are from a legitimate source and will cooperate with any notary, bank, or counsel inquiry.

If Financing is Bank or Blend, Buyer shall pursue a purchase-money first hipoteca from in the amount of . Buyer shall apply promptly, pursue the loan in good faith, and deliver a copy of the commitment letter to Seller within two Business Days after receipt. If, despite good-faith pursuit, Buyer does not receive a written commitment by , Buyer may terminate on or before that deadline and recover the Deposit. Silence after that deadline waives this contingency. If the lender's appraisal is less than the Purchase Price, Buyer shall within five Business Days elect to add cash, request a price reduction Seller may accept or refuse, or terminate and recover the Deposit. Seller has not promised that Buyer will qualify.

If Financing is Owner or Blend, at Closing title will pass to Buyer by escritura, and Seller will be secured by a civil-law hipoteca recorded in the Registry, not by retention of title. Seller-carried principal is at , maturing . The Parties shall execute a promissory note and an escritura de hipoteca before the Notary at Closing. Buyer shall keep the Property insured and shall pay CRIM when due. Remedies after Closing are as stated in the note and mortgage deed. Foreclosure of a Puerto Rico hipoteca is judicial. A condicion resolutoria or title-retained installment structure is not used unless Additional Terms expressly elect it and counsel drafts it.

If Financing is Blend, the Purchase Price is paid in the combination shown in Purchase Price and Consideration. Default lien stack: the institutional lender holds the first hipoteca in the amount of ; Seller holds the second hipoteca in the amount of . Seller shall execute the lender's commercially reasonable subordination so long as it does not increase the permitted first-lien principal above the stated bank loan amount plus ordinary protective advances. If the institutional loan funds at less than the stated bank amount, the shortfall is applied first as Buyer additional cash, then as an increase in the seller note only with Seller's written consent, then as a price reduction only with Seller's written consent, and otherwise Buyer may terminate and recover the Deposit. Sale, first hipoteca, and second hipoteca shall be authorized in one session so priority is clear on presentation to the Registry. Required tax withholding may apply to deferred note payments as well as cash at Closing.

Appraisal Waived is . If Yes, value is not a Buyer termination right except as the Bank module provides when a lender requires an appraisal. If No, Buyer may terminate and recover the Deposit if a licensed appraisal delivered before Closing concludes that as-is market value is less than ninety-five percent of the Purchase Price and the Parties do not agree in writing on a reduced price or credit within three Business Days.

Buyer may obtain a new survey at Buyer's cost, with objections due by . A survey objection is a title objection if it shows an encroachment, lack of record access, a material cabida variance, or an improvement outside the Registry bounds. If Buyer does not order a new survey, Buyer accepts the risk of a Registry-versus- occupation discrepancy, which is not rare in Culebra.

Buyer may inspect the Property, at Buyer's cost, through (the "Inspection Period"). Buyer may inspect structure, roof, electrical, plumbing, cistern or well, septic, solar and batteries, generator, included appliances, wood-destroying organisms, and dock or shoreline works. A Material Defect is a condition that is not readily visible, that materially and adversely affects safety, structure, weather-tightness, or permitted use, and that will cost more than one percent of the Purchase Price to repair as estimated in writing by a licensed contractor or inspector. Buyer shall give written notice of claimed Material Defects before the Inspection Period expires. Seller shall within five Business Days elect to repair, credit, or refuse. If Seller refuses and the Parties do not agree, Buyer may terminate within three Business Days and recover the Deposit, or proceed as-is. Failure to give timely notice waives inspection as a termination right. Buyer shall restore any disturbance caused by inspection.
Optional deal-specific financing notes (commitment letter reference, points cap, balloon, prepayment, or lender name if not captured above).
Additional negotiated terms of the transaction. Handwritten or typed terms here control printed sections if initialed by Buyer and Seller.
Special conditions negotiated by the parties.

Unless a signed post-closing occupancy addendum states otherwise, Seller shall deliver exclusive possession at Closing, broom-clean, free of occupants and of personal property not included in Additional Terms. Keys, codes, cistern and generator instructions, and access devices shall be delivered at Closing. Vacation reservations after the Effective Date require Buyer's written consent.

All fixtures permanently attached to the Property are included, including solar arrays, inverters, batteries hard-wired to the house, antennas, and built-in audiovisual racks. Appliances, furnishings, vehicles, vessels, and other personal property are included only if listed in Additional Terms. Seller shall not remove included items after the Effective Date and shall maintain them in present condition, ordinary wear excepted.

section.title: Condition of Property and Seller Representations

form.section: Except as required by law and except for the representations in this section and any written Seller disclosure, the Property is sold in its present as-is condition. Seller represents, as of the Effective Date and again as of Closing: Seller is the Registry owner or is otherwise authorized to convey; Seller has not granted an unrecorded option, right of first refusal, or lease except as disclosed; to Seller's actual knowledge there is no pending condemnation, code-enforcement, environmental, or coastal-zone proceeding; to Seller's actual knowledge Seller has disclosed material defects of which Seller is actually aware and that a visual inspection would not reveal; improvements made by Seller were made with such permits as applicable law required except as disclosed; there are no occupants except as disclosed; and Seller is not a debtor in a pending bankruptcy that would stay this sale. These representations survive Closing for twelve months. Actual knowledge means the present conscious awareness of the individual signatory.

Buyer may inspect the Property within forty-eight hours before Closing to confirm that it is in substantially the same condition as on the Effective Date, ordinary wear excepted, that included items remain, and that agreed repairs are complete. The walkthrough is not a second inspection contingency.

Taxes, rents if any, HOA dues, utilities, and similar recurring charges shall be prorated as of the Closing Date. Prepaid items and transferable deposits shall be credited accordingly. The Parties shall reprorate within sixty days after Closing if a bill that was estimated is later issued. This clause survives Closing.

If the Property is subject to a homeowners, horizontal-property, or similar regime, Seller shall deliver current governing documents, budget, and a statement of account or estoppel. Buyer shall apply for membership if the regime requires an application. Unpaid assessments for which Seller is responsible shall be paid at Closing. The association's consent is a condition only if the recorded regime actually requires consent to transfer.

Seller shall maintain utility service through Closing. Buyer shall arrange transfer effective the Closing Date. Outstanding charges through Closing remain Seller's responsibility. The Parties shall cooperate on transfer of electric or off-grid systems, generator fuel, propane, water, cistern service, internet or satellite, and any transferable dock or mooring permit.

Each Party may retain independent counsel. Closing shall be conducted before a Puerto Rico notary public. The Notary is not counsel for either Party. Notarial and Registry fees are allocated under Closing Costs. A Party appearing by attorney-in-fact shall deliver the poder in time for the Notary to examine it. Electronic signature of this private contract does not replace the notarial formalities of the escritura or hipoteca.

A transfer of Puerto Rico real property can trigger withholding under the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Code on certain sales by nonresidents of Puerto Rico, and federal FIRPTA withholding if the transferor is a foreign person for U.S. tax purposes. Rates and bases differ. Buyer can be personally liable for a required amount that is not withheld. Seller shall certify residency and FIRPTA status before Closing. Escrow Holder or the Notary shall withhold and remit as counsel and the applicable forms then require. If any part of the Purchase Price is paid after Closing under owner financing, Buyer shall withhold from each later payment to the extent the statute requires. This clause survives Closing.

Buyer may not assign this Agreement without Seller's prior written consent, except to an entity that Buyer controls. Buyer shall give notice of a permitted assignment and deliver the entity's authority documents before the Notary prepares the escritura. No assignment releases Buyer. Seller may not assign except to an entity that assumes all Seller obligations in writing.

Buyer acknowledges that Culebra property can be affected by coastal-zone regulation, public-beach access, mangrove and wildlife rules, FEMA flood mapping, and storm risk. Seller makes no representation about future buildability, shoreline position, or insurance availability except as stated in Condition of Property. Buyer is advised to obtain flood-zone determination and independent insurance quotes during the Inspection Period. Seller shall disclose known unregistered or unpermitted work.

Either Party may structure its side as an exchange under Internal Revenue Code section 1031 or any Puerto Rico analog. The other Party shall cooperate at no material cost or delay and shall not be required to take title to other property.

The brokers named in this Agreement are (Buyer's broker) and (Seller's broker). Commission is earned and paid under separate listing and buyer-representation agreements. Each Party represents it has not engaged another broker whose claim would be a lien on the Deposit or the Property.

If a natural-person Party dies or becomes legally incapacitated before Closing, this Agreement binds the estate or representative. If a named storm warning, earthquake, epidemic restriction, or government closure of the Registry or notaries prevents Closing on the Closing Date, the Closing Date moves to the third Business Day after the impediment lifts, but not later than thirty days after the original Closing Date. After that outside date either Party not then in default may terminate and the Deposit shall be refunded. Financial inability is not force majeure.

All notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, recognized overnight courier, or email with a PDF attached, to the addresses the Parties provide in Additional Terms or on the signature page. Email notice sent before 6:00 p.m. Atlantic Time on a Business Day is effective that day unless the sender receives an automated failure message. Informal messaging applications are not notice unless Additional Terms say they are.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Exclusive venue lies in the Court of First Instance of Puerto Rico. Before filing a damages action, the Parties shall attend a half-day mediation in Puerto Rico or by video, except that a Party may go directly to court for specific performance, injunctive relief, or interpleader. The prevailing Party in a final judgment is entitled to reasonable attorneys' fees and costs.
This Agreement, including any addenda signed by Buyer and Seller, constitutes the entire agreement and supersedes all prior negotiations. Amendments must be in writing and signed by Buyer and Seller.

This Agreement may be signed in counterparts. Electronic delivery of a signed counterpart is effective for this private contract. The escritura de compraventa, mortgage deed, and other notarial instruments must be authorized with the formalities of the Notarial Law.

If any provision is held unenforceable, the remainder continues in effect. The unenforceable provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable. A liquidated-damages clause held to be a penalty is severed without voiding the sale covenants.

Time is of the essence. Business Day means a day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Deadlines that fall on a weekend or legal holiday run to the next Business Day. Atlantic Time controls.
